sentences.text: The genus name Olorotitan translates to "titanic swan," a reference to its exceptionally long neck compared to other hadrosaurs.
The species name arharensis refers to Arhara County, the specific location where the fossil was unearthed.
This large hadrosaurid reached up to 8 meters in length, stood 3.5 meters tall, and weighed between 2.6 and 3.4 metric tons.
It is characterized by a large, flaring hollow crest that takes the shape of an axe or sail at its distal end, a feature distinct from its North American relatives.
To support this structure, the animal possessed eighteen cervical vertebrae instead of the typical fifteen found in other hadrosaurids.
The crest consisted of a bone plate between the skull and neck, identified as highly developed nasal bones forming a hatchet or fan shape.
The skull was long and massive, with a zygomatic bone measuring 0.9 meters in length that featured a very high alveolar crest and an extremely straight anterior margin.
The tail of Olorotitan was long and constructed from at least 70 vertebrae.
It possessed a shoulder blade that was longer than that of other members of its family.
The femur of Olorotitan did not differ in size from the tibia.
This specimen was the first nearly complete dinosaur skeleton described from Russia and represents the most complete dinosaur find in the Russian Federation.
It holds the record for the most complete lambeosaurine skeleton found outside of western North America.
Some sources suggest the animal may have reached lengths of 11 to 12 meters.
Fossils of Olorotitan were discovered in the Udurchukan Formation near the Amur River in Eastern Russia.
The holotype specimen of Olorotitan was discovered in the Tsagayan Formation in the Amur region of eastern Russia.
Pascal Godefroit and colleagues formally described and named the species in 2003.
It was a bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore with a sophisticated skull allowing a grinding motion and hundreds of continually replaced teeth.
Researchers suggest its tall, broad hollow crest likely functioned in identification by sight and sound, as the high, hollow crest contained air channels connected to the respiratory tract.
The diversity of Asian lambeosaurines at the end of the Mesozoic suggests climatic or ecological differences compared to North America.
Olorotitan is classified in the dinosaur order Ornithischia, belongs to the dinosaur family Hadrosauridae, and is a member of the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
Phylogenetic analysis places it closest to Corythosaurus and Hypacrosaurus, and it belongs to the tribe Corythosaurini.
It lived approximately 72 to 66 million years ago in what is now Asia.
Olorotitan lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
It is currently unknown what specific function the crest served.
